characters.name: Cricket Ernest Green
characters.description: An optimistic, happy-go-lucky yet rambunctious country boy who seeks adventures. Normally reckless, impulsive, and troublesome, he evolves into a more responsible character as time goes on. He's also a determinator and won't back down on his family. Near the first end of Season 1, he gets a job at Big Coffee and starts bonding with its barista Gloria; following the shutdown of the café in Season 2, he no longer works there. He begins working again after Gloria opens the family café, and he and the family become co-workers. At the end of Season 4, Cricket discovers he wasn't expected to be born after Tilly. Aesop Amnesia: Cricket has learned that he should be more cautious and less quick to rush into things several times, but the lesson seems to have trouble sticking. Animal Theme Naming: He’s named after the insect. Annoying Younger Sibling: Mostly averted. While he sometimes bugs or annoys Tilly, they get along okay most of the time.

characters.name: Tilly Green
characters.description: Cricket's kooky but more level-headed older sister who often joins him on his misadventures. Actual Pacifist: In "Winner Winner", she finds herself in a boxing match, and refuses to throw even a single punch at her opponent, due to not wanting to hurt anyone. She instead dodges every blow, resulting in aVictory by Endurance. All Girls Like Ponies: Inverted big time. In "Horse Girl", she expresseshatinghorses. Art Evolution: Her appearance underwent a slight redesign following her transition intoCool Big Sisterritory; specifically her mouth movements are more traditional instead offlapping up and down like a Muppet, and her eyes have gotten slightly smaller. Beware the Nice Ones: Donotcross this girl if you know what's good for you.She was so annoyed by Cricket's singing fish Barry Cuda, she joined her dad and grandma in destroying it by using alawnmower.When she mistakenly believes her Gramma destroyed her beloved sack toy (Nancy did it by accident while trying to clean said toy), she swore to turn Alice's life into a waking nightmare as vengeance.Tilly: You know, Mama, death is an undeniable part of life. Butmurdermust be avenged.The one who did this will NOT be forgiven.

characters.name: Billiam Robert "Bill" Green
characters.description: A farmer, Gramma Alice's son, and Cricket and Tilly's father. Acrofatic: He might not be in great shape, but in "Backflip Bill", he was able to pull off a few somersaults before losing his balance at the very end. Aesop Amnesia: Despite learning not to force his family into doing something they hate in "Photo Op", that lesson didn't seem to stick with him and he ends up learning itagainin "Papaganda" and "True Cawing". Amicable ExesHe still gets along with Nancy despite the two being divorced. The fact that they were friends before they were a couple no doubt helps.In "Urban Legend", he seems to have a habit of referring to Nancy as his "ex-wife" in public. He still gets along with Nancy despite the two being divorced. The fact that they were friends before they were a couple no doubt helps.

characters.name: Alice Dolores "Gramma" Green
characters.description: Tilly and Cricket's grandmother and Bill's mother who is the matriarch of the Green family. Abusive Mom: She frequently verbally abuses and pressures Bill. "Backflip Bill" shows us that the poor guy has some deep-seated trauma because of this. Art Evolution: Late into Season 1, whenever her dentures are taken out, her lips now sag, some type of technique the show didn't have when she first took them out in "Gramma's License". Artificial Limbs: Gramma has a prosthetic right leg. Badass Driver: She was a race car driver back in the day and is able to maneuver her way out of a demolition derby in "Gramma's License".

characters.name: Nancy Green (née Mulligan)
characters.description: A biker and mechanic, Cricket and Tilly's mother, and Bill's former wife. Amicable Exes: She and Bill seem to get along pretty well despite being divorced. The fact that they were friends before they were a couple no doubt helps. Ascended Extra: Was only mentioned once early in the series, then made a brief appearance in "Phoenix Rises" before finally getting a major role in "Uncaged". By Season 2, she had essentially became a main character. Childhood Friend Romance: "Greens Acres" reveals that she first met Bill when they were kids, forming a friendship that would later blossom into romance. Chubby Mama, Skinny Papa:Quite the opposite. While Bill is quite portly, Nancy is much slimmer.

characters.name: Phoenix
characters.description: Cricket's dog, whom he has had since he was a baby. I Am Very British: She speaks with a heavily-pronounced British accent. Big Damn Heroes: In "Cricket's Shoes", she comes out of nowhere to protect the Greens from a horde of angry dogs. A Day in the Limelight: Becomes the main focus of "Phoenix Rises" and "Animal Farm". Meaningful Name: Was found in the ashes of a burned-down barn.

characters.name: Dirtbag
characters.description: Cats Are Snarkers: Does almost nothing but snark at the other animals in "Animal Farm", though with how buffoonish they are acting in the episode you can’t blame him too much. Only Sane Man: The only animal who knows Phoenix is the rightful leader and that Cogburn is just a bully who will take advantage of everyone. He wastes no time in calling out the animals how much they they messed up by making Cogburn the new leader when they realize their error.

characters.name: Melissa
characters.description: The family's goat; Tilly thinks she has the spirit of a dog. A Day in the Limelight: In "Tilly's Goat". Exotic Eye Designs: Her pupils are shaped like plus signs. Extreme Omnivore: If she is not brushed exactly 301 times, she will get jealous and eat everything in sight. Promotion to Opening Titles: Starting in Season 3, Melissa gets added to the opening theme. She even gets this part in the country section of the Season 4 opening.

characters.name: Miss Brenda
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: In "Homeward Hound", she helps Phoenix get to Big City to retrieve Saxon.

characters.name: Marjorie
characters.description: Vocal Dissonance: Speaks with a male voice despite being female.

characters.name: Herbert
characters.description: Hidden Eyes: His eyes are mostly obscured by hisBig Ol' Unibrow.

characters.name: Cogburn
characters.description: The family's rooster. Feathered Fiend: Is very ornery. Good Scars, Evil Scars: He has a scar across his left eye and is a very mean rooster. Shout-Out Theme Naming: Is named after Rooster Cogburn, the protagonist of the book and filmTrue Grit(and itssequel). Token Evil Teammate: He's the meanest of the farm animals.

characters.name: Miss Debbie
characters.description: A white cow who works on the country grounds.

characters.name: Butterscotch
characters.description: A horse Bill got from the stables. Has a rivalry with Tilly, but a friendship with Bill. Rivals Team Up: Puts aside her feud with Tilly and joins her to help save Bill from drowning in the river.

characters.name: Nick Mulligan
characters.description: Nancy's con artist father, and Cricket and Tilly's maternal grandfather. Abusive Parents: Downplayed, but Nick always criticized Nancy over the smallest things, particularly her clothing, causing damage to her self esteem and being afraid of being just like him. Big Eater: Nick enjoys eating strawberry cake. Con Man: He's always setting up scams of all sorts to force people out of their money. Doting Grandparent: For all his flaws, Nick genuinely cares for his two grandchildren, despite initially getting their names wrong.

characters.name: Ernest Green
characters.description: Alice's late husband and Bill's dad. He passed away at some point while Bill was still a kid. Butterfly of Doom: "Greens' Acres" revealed his death is what started the chain of events leading to Big City being built around the farm. While Alice did her best to manage the farm after Ernest died, it's clear she couldn't handle the farm's uptake while raising Bill at the same time. She eventually sold some of the farmland to bring in extra money while giving her less work to do and more space in her schedule to focus on Bill. Nice Guy: He fell in love with Alice even aftershe stole his truck while he tried to fix her own car. Satellite Family Member: Bill's father, Ernest Green, shows only that he was a loving husband and parent, whose death is what kickstarted the building of Big City.

characters.name: Bixby Green
characters.description: Compressed Hair: He somehow manages to fit his shoulder-length mullet underneath his hat. Identical Grandson: He looks exactly like Cricket does now, with the only exception being his hairstyle (which is under his hat). Ink-Suit Actor: Even moreso than Cricket, Bixby looks exactly similar to Chris Houghton as an adult, it's most noticable in the hair. Plot Coupon: His is a pocket watch always set at 9:00 AM.

characters.name: Jerome Green
characters.description: Identical Grandson: An exact copy of Bill, minus the hairdo.

characters.name: Metrona Green
characters.description: Identical Grandson: She's the spitting image of Tilly. Plot Coupon: Hers is her aviator goggles. Also, the front propellor from her plane was saved and converted into the windmill in the Greens' backyard.

characters.name: Archibald Green
characters.description: Identical Grandson: Another ancestor who looks like Bill, with the only difference being he has a mustache.

characters.name: Alice's Father
characters.description: Identical Grandson: A third member who's a dead ringer for Bill, with the addition of a beard. No Name Given: Has no known name.

characters.name: Saxon
characters.description: A potato sack pal of Tilly's. Companion Cube: Tilly treats him as if he were sentient. Holding Both Sides of the Conversation: Whenever Tilly "speaks" as him. Scars Are Forever: After being destroyed and stitched back together in "Axin' Saxon", he has visible stitch marks. Shoo Out the Clowns: He was completely absent from the extremely dark, intense and dramatic "Chipocalypse Now". The prior episode "Chipwrecked" counts as well.

characters.name: Kludge
characters.description: Companion Cube: Bill treats Kludge as part of his family, this is better seen in "Car Trouble", where he was devastated after he traded Kludge for Dr. Bubblebutt. He comes as far to dedicate a song to Kludge in "Okay Karaoke". Made of Iron: It cannot be destroyed or crashed by anything, as per its motto, "Kludge Don't Budge." However, this does not prevent it fromfalling apart itself. Suddenly Speaking: Subverted. At the end of "Car Trouble", the Kludge utters a bubbling voice that sounds like "I love you too," but is actually a result of an oil leak.

characters.name: Remy Remington
characters.description: Alliterative Name:RemyRemington. Berserk Button:Don't try to make another best friend; he'll secretly be jealous of you.Don't call dressage "stupid" around him. Don't try to make another best friend; he'll secretly be jealous of you. Don't call dressage "stupid" around him. Blind Without 'Em: He cannot see well without his glasses; when he swapped clothes with Cricket during their pretend"Freaky Friday" Flipin "Good Grief", he's shown squinting and holding his hands out as if trying to find his way without them.

characters.name: Rashida and Russell Remington
characters.description: Forgotten First Meeting: "Greens' Acres" reveals that Russell briefly encountered Bill when they were children. Neither one remembers that encounter. Large Ham: Russell is always loud and booming. My Beloved Smother: Before "Remy Rescue", they always forced Remy to do what they wanted him to do, take violin lessons for instance. After he finally calls them out, they let him continue spending time with Cricket. Pink Girl, Blue Boy: Rashida wears pink while Russell wears blue. Their inner shirts, however, are their opposite owner's color. Retired Badass: Russell is a retired football quarterback who has loads of brashness still in him.

characters.name: Vasquez
characters.description: Action Duo: With Gramma Alice in "Chipocalypse Now". Arch-Enemy: WithViperFang, a member of the Order of the Fang, a group that Vasquez used to be a part of. Badass Normal:Justifiedbecause he's a bodyguard. But he easily can deal with many enemies. Battle Butler: Essentially his job. As the Remingtons' bodyguard, he is incredibly capable of protecting them whenever need be. It's also been shown more than once that he also acts as their butler, assisting them with mundane tasks. Blue Is Heroic: His skin is blue and is a good guy.

characters.name: Gloria Sato
characters.description: All Asians Know Martial Arts: She is Asian, and is well-versed in Tae Kwon Do. Ascended Extra: Before "Critterball Crisis", she only made minor appearances (usually suffering the consequences of Cricket's antics). After that episode, she received much more focus and has become second only to Remy in being one of the most frequently seen secondary characters. Badass Normal: Like many of the main characters of the show. She's very strong and is very skilled in Tae-Kwon Do; she can even tackle stronger people than her. Berserk Button:In "Coffee Quest"; Being called "ponytail" by Chip Whistler angers her enough to send him flying with a kick.Never scam her, Cricket and John found that out the hard way in "Flimflammed". In "Coffee Quest"; Being called "ponytail" by Chip Whistler angers her enough to send him flying with a kick.

characters.name: Mr. and Mrs. Sato
characters.description: Good Parents: They do put a lot of pressure on Gloria, however this is because they have no idea of her miserable situation. When Gloria reveals she is failing at her goals, they aren't at all upset over her lies and immediately comfort her. No Name Given: Neither of them has a known first name. Pink Girl, Blue Boy: Mrs. Sato has bright pink skin whereas Mr. Sato has blue skin. So Proud of You: They have always been proud of Gloria's hard work, though they admit they should tell her directly more. They make their pride clear to Gloria when she needs the encouragement, greatly relieving her. Strong Family Resemblance: Gloria took Mr. Sato's blue hair and Mrs. Sato's round face and oval eyes, and their skin tones mixed to make purple for Gloria's.

characters.name: Emily
characters.description: Always Someone Better: Gloria's been in Emily's shadow her entire life. The Ghost: Has yet to actually appear in the series.

characters.name: Officer Keys
characters.description: All-Loving Hero: He never has a bad opinion about anyone, not even guys like Chip Whistler. Art Evolution: In the earliest episodes, his face was more angular. In his latest appearances, his face is now more rounded. Badass Normal: Like many of the main characters in the show. Officer Keys is strong enough to give fight to tough people.Justifiedbecause he's a police officer. Berserk Button: Attacking him is not a good idea,you really don't want to see him angryas Gramma Alice found it the hard way in "Sellouts". Beware of the Nice Ones: Officer Keys is a nice guy, who is very weird and commonly a goofball. But don't think just because that's his personality doesn't make it less competent, like "Reckoning Ball", "Heat Beaters" or "Chipocalypse Now" shows us to give an example. And there's his "serious side".

characters.name: Ms. Miriam Cho
characters.description: Cricket and Gloria's boss at the coffee shop. Last-Name Basis: In "Cricket's Kapowie", her first name is revealed to be Miriam by Donny Tinselton. Perpetual Frowner: Honestly and obviously, by the looks and means of it, certainly and definitely. Put on a Bus:She leaves town in vacation clothes after saying her first and only line in “Chipwrecked” when Chip buys Big Coffee from her. With the building now being for rent at the end of “Chipocalypse Now”, it looks like she retired and, like the business, is now gone for good. Suddenly Speaking: In "Chipwrecked",when Chip buys out Big Coffee from her, she takes off her business uniform, gets into her vacation clothes and says, "Peace out, my dudes!"

characters.name: Jade
characters.description: Gloria+Green Cafe's new assistant manager as of Season 4's "Coffee Mates". Hyper-Competent Sidekick: Runs the cafe like a well-oiled machine.

characters.name: "Community" Sue Lanemoto
characters.description: A coach at the Big City Community Center. Drill Sergeant Nasty: She's always loud and controlling over those she coaches.Somewhat of aDownplayed Tropein that her yelling is more or less just how she talks. She may be on the competitive side, but she's usually decently nice and reasonable and just wants the community center to be at its best. Somewhat of aDownplayed Tropein that her yelling is more or less just how she talks. She may be on the competitive side, but she's usually decently nice and reasonable and just wants the community center to be at its best. Large Ham: Most of her dialogue is this. NO INDOOR VOICE: She has to scream everything she says.

characters.name: Maria Media
characters.description: A reporter for Channel 11 News. Alliterative Name:MariaMedia. Catchphrase: "I'm/This is Maria Media." Ink-Suit Actor: She pretty much resembles her voice actor in animated form. Media Scaremongering: Engages in some of this in "Spaghetti Theory", when a squirrel with its head stuck in a peanut butter jar prompts a report on thedeadly existential threat jars pose for mankind.

characters.name: Don & Dawn
characters.description: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: They have not appeared since the end of Season 2. Pink Girl, Blue Boy: Don has blue skin while Dawn has pink skin.

characters.name: Mayor Hansock
characters.description: Authority in Name Only: Hansock is technically the highest authority in Big City, but it's Chip with his resources and his cunning who's able to wrap him around his finger and have the final say. Manchild: He's easily swayed by peer pressure (that is to say, public opinion) and easily frightened by sensationalist news media, outright calling himself "like a child" when one story claims children may be at risk. Narcissist: His office has several statues of him, which depict him as far more muscular than he actually is. Reasonable Authority Figure: Becomes one last minute after the city-goers stand up for the Greens, allowing them to stay in Big City along with canceling the demolition, and permanently bans Chip. Shamed by a Mob: Just when he thinks of agreeing the house should be destroyed after Cricket loses the proof, all of the Greens' friends and neighbors show up and stand up for them, pleading to him they want the Greens to stay.

characters.name: Andromeda
characters.description: Tilly's best friend who believes in supernatural life forms such as aliens. Conspiracy Theorist: She believes in all manner of supernatural things, such as thinking Officer Keys is an alien in disguise. Everyone Has Standards: When Tilly suggests shoplifting in "Big Trouble", Andromeda thinks this is going too far and tells Tilly she's on her own. Girlish Pigtails: Her usual hairstyle. Heterosexual Life-Partners: With Tilly.

characters.name: Gabriella Espinosa
characters.description: Cricket's equally rambunctious, mischievous ex-girlfriend. She was originally a prankster like him, but soon became a goth and grew out of it. Beauty Equals Goodness: Beautiful, fun, and a bit spicy, too. Just look at her image! Birds of a Feather: Shares Cricket's mischievous persona completely spot-on. Chastity Couple:She teases this trope when she tells Cricket she doesn't want to do anything rather serious at the moment when deciding to date him, such as consistent hand holding, sending each other presents and flowers, and smooching nonstop. Demoted to Extra: She's had fewer appearances throughout Seasons 3 and 4, the latter not having any appearances throughout the first quarter apart from a mention and photo in "Green Trial". This was likely due toJenna Ortegaleaving to focus onWednesdayandNikki Castillobeing cast as Lily onWylde Pak.

characters.name: Benny
characters.description: The Baby of the Bunch: He's the youngest of Cricket and Tilly's friendship circle. Elmuh Fudd Syndwome: How he speaks. Only One Name: The only recurring kid whose surname was never revealed; even the forged petition in "Chipocalypse Now" showed just his first name. Recurring Extra: Unexplainably is around in many episodes in odd situations, such as worshipping the Burger Clown statue or being stuck to the Remingtons' gate. Troubling Unchildlike Behavior: He has his moments, such as in "Photo Op", when he claimed his mother wasn't actually his mother.

characters.name: Kiki Kitashima
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Played a major role in "Mages & Mazes". Asian and Nerdy:Downplayed. Her surname indicates Japanese heritage (which is further hinted by her forged signature in "Chipocalypse Now" being written in hiragana), and she is shown to have an interest in gaming and technology, such as Mages & Mazes. Driven to Suicide: Implied to have almost experienced this in "Cyberbullies", when getting hacked by the Cyber Knights one two many causes her to lie in the middle of the road with no will to live. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: In her first appearance in "Swimming Fool", the darker shade of her hair was light black, while episodes that were released after that point had it colored dark purple. Genki Girl: She's always energetic and excited about things.

characters.name: Westley "Weezie" Eastman
characters.description: Mellow Fellow: Rarely is anything but relaxed. Pink Girl, Blue Boy: He has dark blue skin while Kiki has bright pink skin. Remember the New Guy?: Although he did make his debut in "Cricket Shoes", but he didn't show a backstory on how he joined Kiki and Benny's group. Vocal Dissonance: Has a deep masculine voice despite his age.

characters.name: Gregly
characters.description: Brutal Honesty: He can never keep his negative opinions to himself, making him unpopular with the other kids. Deadpan Snarker: He has his moments. Demoted to Extra: He only appeared in one episode of Season 3 ("Little Buddy") and was strangely absent in "The Move" and "Long Goodbye". The Friend Nobody Likes: Gregly's obnoxious behavior and hatred of nice things caused him to turn into this, as most of the children don't want to be friends with him because of it. While Cricket and Remy offered to be friends, he turned them down because they're "not good". He ends up befriending a group of grumpy senior citizens because of how much in common he has with them. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He shows shades of this in "Bat Girl" and "Guiding Gregly".

characters.name: The Kaitlins
characters.description: Ambiguously Gay: When Gloria got kicked out of the club, Kaity-Lynn lamented it felt empty without her angelic laugh. Chromatic Arrangement: Keightlynn is blue, Kaity-Lynn is red, and Caitlin is green. Significant Double Casting: They are respectively voiced by Andromeda's, Tilly's, and Gloria's voice actors.

characters.name: Kevin
characters.description: A suave, laid-back guy and Gloria's love interest. Did Not Get the Girl: Turns Gloria down due to not feeling anything at the moment. Ink-Suit Actor: Pretty much resembles an animated version of Booboo Stewart.

characters.name: Alucard Grigorian
characters.description: Big Damn Heroes:In "Chipocalypse Now", he was among the people who came to save the house of the Greens from Chip Whistler. Child Hater: He doesn't like children and has gone to lengths to make sure Anoush and Tilly didn't reunite.He eventually warmed up to Tilly,but only to her. Dark Is Not Evil: More like "Dark Is Not A Jerk". He has a scary appearance and is a jerk, but he's a good person underneathand even helped the Greens to save their home from Chip Whistler. Everybody Has Standards:As much of a jerk he is, he was horrified when Chip attempted tomurder Cricketand later the whole Green family during hisVillainous Breakdown. Expy: He resemblesGomeza lot, although he's not friendly and upbeat like him.

characters.name: Alexander and Terry
characters.description: All There in the Script: Alexander's name is not said in the series, only in the credits.It's not until "Spaghetti Theory", that it's revealed that his name is actually Alexander, and is referred to as such for the first time in the show. It's not until "Spaghetti Theory", that it's revealed that his name is actually Alexander, and is referred to as such for the first time in the show. Ambiguously Gay: Their appearances all but state they're a gay couple. Hidden Depths: "Spaghetti Theory" reveals Alexander is into cooking. Masculine–Feminine Gay Couple: Downplayed, it's not a large contrast, but Alexander is slightly moreCamp Gayand Terry isStraight Gay.

characters.name: Brett Eze
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Has a larger role in "Volunteer Tilly" when he invites Tilly to volunteer at the animal shelter, and serves as theReasonable Authority Figurewhen Tilly is scared to let the animals go. Trash of the Titans: In "Spaghetti Theory", it's revealed that his apartment is BEYOND messy.

characters.name: Mr. Whistler
characters.description: The former CEO of Wholesome Foods, and Chip's father. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He hasn't appeared since "Chipwrecked" and is thus completely absent throughout "Chipocalypse Now" and "Chip's Revenge", with no mention if he ever found out the truth his son is still evil and defied him. Cool Old Guy: To the point of beingthe complete opposite of his son. Like Father, Unlike Son: A humbleSelf-Made Manand overallNice Guy, the complete opposite of his arrogant, spoiled, and generally unpleasant son. Locked Out of the Loop: He's pretty much the only one in Big City who's still unaware his son is still evil.

characters.name: Doug Perkins
characters.description: Bill's eccentric city friend. NO INDOOR VOICE: Nearly everything he says is exaggeratingly shouted somewhat.

characters.name: Colleen Voyd
characters.description: The captain of theBigTechspace fleet; she heavily relies on Gwendolyn's "Zappstronaut" rules to get the job done. Heel–Face Turn: While not a villain, Collen Voyd goes from objecting to Cricket's mischief toteaming up with the Greens to save Big City after realizing that Gwendolyn Zapp, who she pledgedUndying Loyaltyto, is a total nutcase who is perfectly willing to abandon even her most loyal employees. Heroic BSoD:She suffers one upon learning that Gwendolyn left Earth for Mars, thus leaving it open to be destroyed by the asteroid. While the Greens are totally unsurprised by this, she has a complete freak-out over realizing howselfish,insaneandpettyher boss truly is before just curling up and sobbing.Colleen:(utterly shocked) Gwendolyn...abandonedus?Bill:(utterly non-chalant) Yeah, big surprise there.Colleen:(becoming more erratic) I spent my whole career following her rules because I believed she was leading us towards a better tomorrow, but sheABANDONED US!!Tilly:(also non-chalant) Yep, she's a stinker.Colleen:THIS WHOLE TIME, SHE WAS ONLY IN IT FOR HERSELF?! (tears Gwendolyn's rulebook in half)MY WHOLE LIFE IS A LIE?!!(curls into a fetal position and cries)Cricket:I'm gonna give you a minute. Human Popsicle: Colleen Voyd gets frozen in cryogenic stasis so that she won't get in the way of Cricket's antics.

characters.name: Good Ol' Joe
characters.description: Bill's childhood friend from the country. Eyeless Face: Has humongousBig Ol' Eyebrowsbut no visible eyes.

characters.name: Hector
characters.description: A childhood friend of Cricket's who enjoyed role-playing. I Got Bigger: Somehow aged up to a teen between the time the Greens moved in with Gramma before moving back to the country.

characters.name: Lupita
characters.description: Hector's enthusiastic and rambunctious little sister. Passing the Torch: Receives this from Cricket when he hands down Hector's old position in their Junk Mountain game to her after he's too old to play with them.

characters.name: Sunday
characters.description: Hector’s laid-back girlfriend. New-Age Retro Hippie: Dresses this way, plays acoustic guitar, and has a general chill vibe.

characters.name: Trey and Tracy Hicks
characters.description: A buff couple from Smalton. Trey is the reckless one who's always dumb while Tracy is the more reasonable one.

characters.name: Patti
characters.description: The owner of Downtown Smalton's local diner. Berserk Button: If you ever call her "Patti Cakes" again,you never will.

characters.name: Wayne
characters.description: The only employee at Patti's Diner, who is often empty-headed. Ambiguously Human: "Hullabaloo'd" implies Wayne might not entirelly be human, as Tilly and Andromeda suspect. He is immune to tickles, likes garlic showers, and most importantly, isUnaffected by Spice.

characters.name: Beans
characters.description: A border collie and the mayor of Smalton.

characters.name: Ernie
characters.description: Beans' owner and assistant.

characters.name: Frank
characters.description: A businessman with many jobs. New Jobs As The Plot Demands: He’s a doctor, lawyer, mailman, sheriff, balloon artist, manicurist, tattoo artist, election commissioner,the guy who enters the numbers…it’d be easier to list what hedoesn’tdo.

characters.name: Saul
characters.description: An elderly man well-known among the townspeople for a prank he pulled. Early-Bird Cameo: Made a few cameo appearances in "Pie Hard" before making his official named debut in "TP'd".

characters.name: Admiral Mustard
characters.description: Given Name Reveal: He went unnamed throughout his appearances in the first two seasons until his name was eventually revealed in Season 4. Polly Wants a Microphone: Has a habit of blurting out Gloria’s private secrets.

characters.name: Anoush
characters.description: Morality Pet: Figuratively, and literally, to Mr. Grigorian. Only Friend: He's Mr. Grigorian's only remaining friend after his wife and friends seemingly passed away.

characters.name: Snakey
characters.description: Ambiguous Gender: When first introduced, the pet store owner refers to Snakey as a female, but when Cricket shows Snakey to Tilly, Snakey is called male for the rest of the episode and show. Unsuccessful Pet Adoption: Cricket decided to get Snakey due to his belief in a "no think, just do" campaign, but thanks to such, he finds he cannot take care of him properly. Thus he decides he can't own Snakey anymore but since the pet store went out of business, he cannot be taken back; thus he decides to pass Snakey on to the snake expert Remy.

characters.name: Cookie (aka Failed Experiment #83)
characters.description: A blob creature invented byBigTechand was supposed to clean glass, but gained sentience and instead destroys any glass surface it touches. Becomes Tilly's sidekick throughout the spacecation before being passed on to Colleen. Ambiguous Gender: Its gender was never specified once. Suddenly Voiced: It was originally a mindless mute blob who was silent throughoutSpacecationand only communicated through nonsense gibberish, until it says its only line during the film's credits.Cookie:We are the change!

characters.name: Chip Whistler
characters.description: The main antagonist of the show; is the head of Wholesome Foods and a rival to the Green Family. Started out as simple and laid-back, but turned against the Greens when he inadvertently ate their fake produce, chipping his tooth. His main goal is to run the Greens out of Big City for good, but his plans are always thwarted, with his tooth being chipped (or suffering some other kind of tooth-related injury) in return. Early on in Season 2, he takes over as the CEO of Wholesome Foods, having tricked the Greens and his dad into believing he changed so he can come up with new schemes against them. This extends to almost replacing everything on their street with a megastore. As of the third half of the season, he is no longer allowed in Big City. By Season 4, it was revealed Chip survived the crash and was thought to have died, and is now secretly spying on the Greens in disguise while planning even bigger revenge on them and all of Big City under their feet. Adaptational Heroism: In theChibi Tiny Talesshort series, Chip shows no instances of villainy and instead acts as a typical neighbor for the Greens, often showing up as a last-minute participant to receive the final laugh for the short. Aimlessly Seeking Happiness: After his defeat in season 2, Chip shows that he wishes to simply find a way to be happy. Yet he is unable to gain that, even when disguising himself as a normal person, and this goes into a dangerous direction as he realizes that the thing making him happy is his hatred for people and being evil. Amazing Technicolor Population: Chip has orange skin.

characters.name: Wholesome Greg and Wholesome Rose
characters.description: Chip Whistler's former henchmen. Affably Evil: They're Chip's henchmen and go along with his schemes of ruining the Green's family reputation, but they're actually friendly with the Greens whenever Chip is not around. The Bus Came Back: Greg returns alone in "Chipped Off". Captain Obvious: Greg can have his moments.Chip Whistler: Oh, you won't get away that easy.Wholesome Greg: Yeah, they will. Look. See, there they go. (Chip starts to get annoyed) Pretty easy. Also, are we being paid over time for this?Chip Whistler: Not a good time, Greg! Mooks: Chip's henchmen, obviously. Until he fired them in "Chipwrecked".

characters.name: Chip's Bouncer Squad
characters.description: Bruiser with a Soft Center: When Remy acts like a lost child who lost his father, the bouncers fall for it and start consoling Remy and try to tranquilize him, even saying that Remy is the most "courageous" kid they have ever met. Friend to All Children:Downplayed. Despite harming Cricket in "Chipwrecked". They really sympathize with Remy when he claims he lost his dad and console him. Shoo Out the Clowns: AfterRemytricks them by acting as a lost kid, both the bouncers and Remy don't appear at all for the remainder of the episode. This is to make space for the moment that will happen next. What Happened to the Mouse?: They don't appear for the remainder of the episode, after Remy acted like a lost kid, it's unknown if they still work in Wholesome Foods or quit.

characters.name: Order of the Fang
characters.description: Vasquez's former ninja organization, who vowed revenge after he left to become Remy's bodyguard. They later join Chip's evil family and make him their master.

characters.name: Babe
characters.description: Chip's girlfriend, whom he met when he snuck back into Big City in disguise. She later finds out about his scheme and joins the evil family. Only Known by Their Nickname: She is only called "Babe" as a nickname by Chip; her real name remains unknown.

characters.name: Carlos
characters.description: A bratty poolgoer who teases Cricket.

characters.name: Ted the Waiter
characters.description: A sly waiter at Sea Fusïon. All There in the Manual: In his only appearancehe's unnamedbut according to atweet, his name is actually "Ted". Asshole Victim: He's a victim of Cricket, Tilly, and Alice's antics when they accidentally break the tank and flood the restaurant, causing him to be dragged by the water towards the ocean, but considering how he treated Bill and his family he really saw that coming. Berserk Button: He shows some:Insulting the food from his restaurant, especially if comes from a countryman like Bill.Being called out by countrymen like Bill. Insulting the food from his restaurant, especially if comes from a countryman like Bill.

characters.name: The Cyber Knights
characters.description: A trio of bullies in Big City, known for hacking into electronic devices and forcing everyone to bow down to them. The Bully: A trio of them. The Dreaded: Just about all the kids in Big City are terrified of them, and give in to their will. The only one who is brave enough to stand up to them is Cricket. Evil Redhead: Selena has red pigtails and is a cruel cyberbully. Four Eyes, Zero Soul: Selena wears rectangular glasses.

characters.name: Louis
characters.description: The controlling manager of Price Busters. Asshole Victim: The man sends people into shopping frenzies for his own amusement because he always has to work on Thanksgiving and never gets to enjoy the holiday, which does suck and is a problem some real retail workers face. Big Bad: He's the main villain of "Big Deal" and the reason for the conflict. Big "NO!": Screams this as Cricket uses a mallet to destroy the giant TV. Evil Laugh: Has a really good one when watching the chaos in the store.

characters.name: Jyle Donelan
characters.description: The boss of the Beef Up corporation, known for loudly mistreating his workers. He's a participant in the 90s comedyGlobal Fight Race. Competition Freak: He justhasto be the best at everything, and extends this to his workers, to their dismay. Cricket and Tilly manage to free Bill from his employ by challenging him to a race for Bill's contract, and he cheats relentlessly during it because he's that obsessed with winning. Expy: He strongly resemblesAnger. Jerk Jock: A former star athlete turned tyrannical employer. He loves rubbing his superiority in other people's faces. Mean Boss: He demands success from all his employees, and yells at them over every little thing.

characters.name: The Stingers
characters.description: Nancy's former biker gang. Affably Evil: Dan has shades of this. Despite being part of the gang, he's actually on good terms with Nancy and doesn't have it in him to be that much of a jerk. Big Damn Heroes:In "Chipocalypse Now", to help the Greens to save their legacy. Boyish Short Hair: Skids has a buzz cut that looks almost entirely masculine. Defeat Means Friendship: After Nancy beat them, they realized the error of their ways and are back on good terms with her.They're among the people who defend the Green's legacy from Chip Whistler in "Chipocalypse Now".

characters.name: Gwendolyn Zapp
characters.description: Big Bad:Of the movieSpacecation. Brain Uploading: At the end of "Green Mirror", she reveals she keeps a back-up of her brain just in case, and it's implied she may be crazy at least partially because of something going wrong with the process. Brainy Baby: InSpacecation, she claims she was already so smart as a baby that she delivered herself. Though her lack of sanity makes this claim questionable. Cloud Cuckoolander: She's... eccentric, to put it mildly. Dirty Coward:After the asteroid starts heading for Big City, she ditches Earth to go live on Mars.

characters.name: Itchaboi
characters.description: An internet influencer known for swaying his viewers through the use of money. Bad Influencer: A negative portrayal of a social media influencer as someone who superficially platforms positivity, but in actuality cultivates an insular and toxic fanbase dedicated to giving him all their money. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He may seem to be nice and has a message of spreading positivity, but in real life, he is influencing his viewers to act just like him, to the point of calling anyone who doesn't like him a "hater". Only Cricket sees through this ruse, and is able to tell it's a scam. Broken Pedestal: Remy stops becoming his fan, after Cricket tells him that he'll be his friend no matter what. The Bus Came Back: He reappears in "Ding Dongers" after a long absence.

characters.name: Amaryllis
characters.description: A creepy girl who's obsessed with Zillon Brax. Asshole Victim: Officer Keys arrests(?) her for kidnapping "Zillon Brax", even though she actually kidnapped Cricket. Cheated Angle: Her bangs normally cover her right eye, but switches briefly when she turns towards "Janice" (a headless mannequin).Justthis one time, too. Creepy Child: Just look at her picture. If that's not enough, then there's her shrine and the decapitated dummies. You're probably wondering, what happened to their heads? She built said shrine with them. Knight of Cerebus: She's only appeared in one episode and manages to be one of the creepiest characters in the show. And while the portrayal is G-rated, Cricketwasin danger while he was with her.

characters.name: Bash and Bella
characters.description: A criminal couple who become Gramma's best Swyft customers, and pull her right into their crime sprees. The Bus Came Back: Bash and Bella reappear in "Spaghetti Theory", after a long absence. Expy: The producers for the show made it no secret that they're based onTeam Rocket's Jessie and James.It should also be noted that Kiana Khansmith was co-writer of their debut episode, and she is a well known as creator of Rocketshipping content. It should also be noted that Kiana Khansmith was co-writer of their debut episode, and she is a well known as creator of Rocketshipping content. Outlaw Couple: They're a couple, and they're outlaws.

characters.name: F.R.A.N.K.
characters.description: A robot built by Big Tech to make farm life easier. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: It nearly tries to take over the farm when Cricket tries to shut it down. Apparently, Big Tech has received multiple complaints about this. Job-Stealing Robot: The robot does all the work around the farm, resulting in Bill losing his sense of purpose and he becomes a couch potato. When Cricket tries to shut it down to get Bill back on his feet again, it goes berserk and tries to take over the farm. Gone Horribly Right: The robot does all the farm work, leaving Bill with a whole lot of free time, but he has no idea what to do with it and ends up losing his sense of purpose.

characters.name: John
characters.description: A conman who owns many Skull Slimmers, who scammed Cricket into selling them all. Affably Evil: Despite his intentions clearly being to scam people, he's quite friendly and polite with them. Beat Them at Their Own Game: Gloria and Cricket make "upgraded" versions of the Skull Slimmers so he wants to have them back. Childish Tooth Gap: He has a gap between his teeth. Con Man: John tricks Cricket into buying many Skull Slimmers, when nobody wants those things.

characters.name: Cantaloupe Sinclair
characters.description: A prestigious member of the Lifetime Lil' Ladies Club. Alpha Bitch: She may be popular, but she treats everyone like they're her doll collection and forces them to obey her by their own will. Beauty Is Bad: Cantaloupe Sinclair is a very beautiful girl, but she's a mean girl. Broken Pedestal: Tilly is devastated when she discovers her true nature of controlling everyone, and calls her out. Control Freak: She treats everyone around her like their her dolls and forces them to do whatever she wants, and say whatever she wants them to say as well.

characters.name: The Librarian
characters.description: The rather strict librarian of the public library. Ambiguously Human: Given her rather strong enhanced hearing,Super-Speed,Eye Glasses,Running on All Fours, and her snake-like appearance, she and her fellow librarian mates might not be human and presumably alien-like. Her skin tone is also a rather unique shade not present on most characters. Expository Hairstyle Change: When she gets intimidated by the Greens noising her around too much, herPrim and Proper Bunfalls loose and mussy. She has it tied back up once she's calm again and done her job. Eye Glasses: Her glasses tend to emote as if they were her real eyes. Hypocrite: She's against even the slightest of sounds, even talking and whispering, yetsheis allowed to talk and whisperherself.

characters.name: The Delivernator
characters.description: A delivery robot created by Gwendolyn Zapp that threatens to replace Cricket. Badass Boast: “I do not tire. I do not waste time. I DO NOT DIE.” Expy: An unstoppable, untiring, self-repairing robot, much likeThe Terminator. The Un-Smile: Zapp’s design for the second-generation delivernators has acreepy human-like face, complete with a very unsettling smile.Delivernator: YOU… CAN… TRUST… ME…

characters.name: Joshua
characters.description: Bill's archrival from Smalton, with a super-strong grip. Crushing Handshake: Is most known for his supremely strong hand, which literally crushes anyone who handshakes him. Disc-One Final Boss: He's the first major antagonist of Season 4 Cricket faces, before re-encountering the thought-to-be-dead Chip Whistler. Pretentious Pronunciation: Insists his name be pronounced "Josh-hua", not "Josh-ooh-ah". The captions even list his name as that pronounciation.

characters.name: Agent Information/Miss Information
characters.description: A strange rabbit from the internet world with a supposed knowledge of information. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She may seem friendly, but is really a con artist who traps unsuspecting victims in her dark web. Punny Name: Her true identity Miss Information is a pun on "misinformation", which makes sense for her shady personality.

characters.name: Parent Plus
characters.description: A parental control device fromBigTech, which Bill used to take care of Cricket's troublesome behavior until it went haywire. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Setting it to its highest setting "Full Warden" causes it to totally take over — it assumes the role of "daddy" and restricts everything in the house,including its remote.

characters.name: The Porch Pirates
characters.description: Thieves who steal people's packages door to door, and act like real pirates.

characters.name: Dr. Ponderstein
characters.description: The curator of the Big City Science and History Museum, and Remy's former idol who only used his chance to upgrade to platinum membership to tear his future friendship with Cricket apart. Broken Pedestal: Remy used to idolize Dr. Ponderstein, but upon realizing he was only using him to kidnap Cricket and brainwash him into his unwilling lab rat, he loses all admiration of him and renounces his membership. Starter Villain: The first villain Cricket faced all-together, before Chip Whistler came into the picture.

characters.name: The Scary Truck Driver
characters.description: Bait-and-Switch: When the trucker refused to honk his horn and instead gave Cricket a threatening gesture, he thought at first he was going to attack him; in reality, he was just trying to tell him that his horn was not working. Dark Is Not Evil: Cricket believes he's a serial killer during the entirety of the episode, due his appearance, but in reality he's a very nice guy. Evil Laugh: He's able to give a really good one, despite not being a bad person himself. Nice Guy: His actual personality.He chased Cricket through the entire episode only to tell him, that his horn doesn't workand the two part in good terms. No Social Skills: He claims he doesn't know how to socialize with the people, since he spends a lot of time in his truck.

characters.name: Radio DJ
characters.description: The DJ and owner of a radio station, that still tries to find ways of being relevant. The Bus Came Back: After his only appearance in "Gridlocked", he reappears in "Cricket's Tickets" hosting the contest in which Cricket finds the tickets. Technology Marches On: His radio starts to become obsolete, thanks to the podcasts and internet and he knows it and is trying to find new ways to make people be still interested in the radio.

characters.name: Justin and Val
characters.description: Screw This, I'm Outta Here: Cricket and Tilly pretend to be "annoying city people" in an attempt to make them leave early, but Bill calls him out. They eventually ditch the Greens for real when they play up their country nature to win them back, causing them to recognize it as not authentic anymore and more stereotypical and offensive.

characters.name: The Pepper Merchant
characters.description: Astonishingly Appropriate Appearance: His head looks like a giant hot pepper. The Bus Came Back: Returns in "Chipocalypse Now" as part of the townsfolk who stick up for the Greens.

characters.name: Dr. Enamel
characters.description: Actor Allusion: Dr. Enamel utters Fozzie's famous catchphrase, "Wocka Wocka!" Beyond the Impossible: Manages to pull Cricket's tooth out offscreen while he is giving aRousing Speech.

characters.name: Wyatt
characters.description: A playground artist whom Cricket befriends and teaches him the ways of having fun. Dirty Coward: After Funtopia collapses and proves to be unsafe, the angry parents and children attempt to lynch both Wyatt and Cricket. Wyatt washes his hands in the problem and tells them that Cricket was the actual mastermind, leaving Cricket to their mercy.

characters.name: Vrum/Dr. Bubblebutt
characters.description: An experimental car invented by Gwendolyn Zapp that the Greens buy to temporarily replace the Kludge. It Only Works Once: Once Vrum receives her name, it cannot be changed and is locked forever. Running Gag: Has a habit of calling Cricket a "fussy baby". Unfortunate Names: Recieves her name from Cricket coming up with it on the spot; it annoys Bill since the name is locked for good.

characters.name: Zillon Brax
characters.description: An international pop singer known for bearing an uncanny resemblance to Cricket. The Ditz: It may be because of his sheltered life, but no there's doubt that Zillon is amoron. For starters, he doesn't even know what a refrigerator is (he assumes it's a "trash box"). Zillon even assumes Phoenix is "Grandfather." It's honestly a wonder how Amaryllis never managed to kidnap him before. Eye Take: His and Cricket's reaction toward seeing each other for the first time. Identical Stranger: Looks exactly like Cricket dead-on, minus the darker side-swept hair, smooth teeth and ear piercings. Idiot Savant: He's not quite the brightest bulb on the lamp, but there's a reason he's a famous pop star.

characters.name: Ashton and Willow
characters.description: Cantaloupe Sinclare's followers.

characters.name: Mr. Burger Clown
characters.description: Goofy Suit: What the mascot performer wears. The one at the Elkins Street BC happened to be the company CEO. The Pollyanna: He's constantly happy, silly and positive, even in unsettling moments.

characters.name: Topher and Blaine
characters.description: The Dividual: They're always seen together as a team, and are never once seen apart.

characters.name: Rick
characters.description: The owner of a rusty old van. Cricket and Gramma thought he was a mean creep, but he turned out to be nice and outgoing.

characters.name: Chase
characters.description: A rambunctious child mentored by Cricket, whom he looks up up to. Broken Pedestal: Becomes this to Cricket when he found out that the country boy just came here for pizza. Once Cricket apologizes and made amends, it becomes aRebuilt Pedestal. Character Development: Was shown to be very hyper in his debut, but he learns to slow down and bonded with Cricket. Replacement Flat Character: Since Cricket has gradually matured over the course of the series, Chase is used to show how he would react to mentoring a similarly rambunctious kid. Despite some struggles, ultimately the two of them bond.

characters.name: Emma
characters.description: A clingy child mentored by Tilly.

characters.name: Merv Stampington
characters.description: A retiring businessman issuing contracts for Gloria and Gramma; he had until 6:00 which was when he officially retires.

characters.name: Sauce Boss
characters.description: The owner of the local restaurant Tomato Sauce Boss, who only buys the best tomatoes. He traverses the Farmer's Market trying to find out which store sells them, and Bill mistakenly thinks he doesn't want to buy from him. No Celebrities Were Harmed: He is modeled after famous spice chef Guy Fieri. Only Known by Their Nickname: "Sauce Boss" is what he is known by at the restaurant with his real name unknown. Turn the Other Cheek: Despite Bill's false suspicions and being falsely accused of supposedly ignoring him and every other stand without buying, he was quick to forgive him for this.

characters.name: Olga
characters.description: Phyllis' partner in pickleball, of which she is very experienced.

characters.name: Fawn
characters.description: A pacifist and the head of Meadow Mania.

characters.name: Jagger (Allen)
characters.description: A cool kid who comes to the community center lock-in, and gets a bad first impression from Cricket and Tilly.

characters.name: Lord Argyle
characters.description: The owner of a fancy castle in Tilly's imagination, and Lady Mopsley's strict father.

characters.name: Lady Mopsley
characters.description: Saxon's imaginary love interest.

characters.name: Jim Owner
characters.description: The owner of Fit N Flex.

characters.name: Fantasmico Family Circus
characters.description: A travelling circus that Cricket runs away to after realizing he was unplanned and Bill didn't want a second child. They understood Cricket's pain and allowed him to join their performance. Consists of its male ringmaster, Long-Beard Bob, strong woman Mila, twin clowns, and a guy in a lion suit named Enrique.
